definition: In machine learning, a nearest centroid classifier or nearest prototype classifier is a classification model that assigns to observations the label of the class of training samples whose mean (centroid) is closest to the observation.
details: When applied to text classification using word vectors containing tf*idf weights to represent documents, the nearest centroid classifier is known as the Rocchio classifier because of its similarity to the Rocchio algorithm for relevance feedback. An extended version of the nearest centroid classifier has found applications in the medical domain, specifically classification of tumors.

explainer.lead: A nearest centroid classifier labels an observation with the class whose training samples' mean is closest to it. It matters as a simple, fast baseline for classification, including text.

tiers.eli5: Imagine plotting each category's average point on a map; a new item gets the label of whichever average point is nearest.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a cheap baseline, and with tf-idf word vectors for text it becomes the Rocchio classifier. A pitfall is that a single mean per class ignores multimodal or spread-out class distributions.
tiers.paperLevel: A nearest centroid classifier assigns each observation the label of the class of training samples whose mean (centroid) is closest. With tf-idf word vectors for text it is known as the Rocchio classifier; extended versions are used for tumour classification.

explainer.example: Documents are vectorised with tf-idf weights; a new article is assigned to whichever class centroid is nearest, as in the Rocchio classifier.
